design_detail: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, within-person laboratory study in 16 healthy volunteers (12 men, 4 women), each attending four sessions at least 14 days apart in counterbalanced order: placebo then placebo; citalopram then placebo; placebo then MDMA; citalopram then MDMA. Citalopram 40 mg (or saline) was given by intravenous infusion over 90 minutes, then MDMA 1.5 mg/kg (mean 100 mg, SD 10) or placebo capsules by mouth. Psychological effects were rated 120 minutes after MDMA with the Altered States of Consciousness Rating Scale (ASC) and the Adjective Mood Rating Scale (AM). Blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, side effects and startle reflex were also recorded and are reported in other papers. No blood levels of MDMA or citalopram were measured.
can_establish: Whether, in 16 healthy volunteers (13 of them with no previous MDMA experience), a single intravenous dose of citalopram 90 minutes before MDMA lowers the psychological effects of MDMA that they rate 2 hours after the MDMA dose (positive mood, derealization, depersonalization, altered sense of time, thought disorder, loss of control, changed meaning of percepts, self-confidence, extroversion), and which ratings are not lowered (emotional excitability, sensitivity).
cannot_establish: What happens in people who take an SSRI by mouth for weeks (steady state) or for illness, at other MDMA doses, with repeated MDMA doses, or in people who regularly take MDMA (only 3 of 16 had tried it); whether MDMA or citalopram blood levels changed (not measured); whether the longer duration of effect after citalopram (about 5 hours against 3) is real, since no measurement method, spread or test is given for it; the cause of the lower ratings beyond the authors' reading that they reflect action at the serotonin uptake site; whether lower ratings lead people to take more MDMA, or what happens to their blood levels if they do (no one took a second dose); sex differences (4 women).

sample.recruitment: Volunteers recruited at the University Hospital and the Medical School of the University of Zurich, informed in writing and orally about the study, MDMA's psychological effects, side effects, previous toxicology and psychiatric risks; written consent. Approved by the Ethics Committee of the Psychiatric University Hospital Zurich and the Swiss Federal Health Office (Materials and Method; Subjects).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Healthy by history, physical examination and blood analysis; psychiatric interview; excluded: major psychiatric disorder in first-degree relatives, head injury, alcohol or regular substance abuse, and a score more than 2 standard deviations above the norm on the neuroticism scale of the Freiburger Personality Inventory.
sample.demographics: 12 men and 4 women, aged 21 to 39 (mean 27.4, SD 4.4); all with high-school education and all but one university students or physicians. Six had previous recreational drug experience: two had tried ecstasy, three a hallucinogen and one both.
sample.attrition: None reported; every analysis has n=16.
sample.selection_effects: Highly educated, screened, mostly drug-naive volunteers (13 of 16 had never taken MDMA), tested once in a hospital; not typical of people who take MDMA at events or of people on long-term antidepressants. The paper itself says the earlier case series of 4 people on fluoxetine differed in dose and route.

exposure.measurement: Citalopram hydrochloride 40 mg ampoules (supplied by Lundbeck, Switzerland) dissolved in 500 mL sterile saline and infused over 90 minutes (330 mL/h); saline alone as placebo; racemic MDMA from the Swiss Federal Health Office in 10 and 50 mg capsules prepared by a hospital pharmacy, and placebo capsules. No concentrations were measured.
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Study conditions only: citalopram 40 mg intravenously once, MDMA 1.5 mg/kg by mouth (mean 100 mg, range about 80 to 120 mg) given after the catheter was removed; a pilot with citalopram 40 to 80 mg before MDMA preceded the study; sessions began at 9 AM or 2 PM.
exposure.polysubstance: No other drug; the volunteers did not eat or drink coffee for 2 hours before each session.
exposure.abstinence_at_testing: Alcohol or regular substance abuse excluded; abstinence before sessions is not described beyond the 2-hour fast.

comparison.controls: Each volunteer's own placebo-placebo, citalopram-placebo and placebo-MDMA sessions, in counterbalanced order, at least 14 days apart.
comparison.matching: Within person; the method of counterbalancing is not described.
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Neuroticism was screened; no genotype (CYP2D6 or serotonin-transporter) and no blood levels.
comparison.controls_other_drug_use: Not applicable beyond the exclusion of substance abuse; six had tried recreational drugs.

outcomes.instruments: Altered States of Consciousness Rating Scale (ASC; 66 visual-analog items in three scales: oceanic boundlessness, anxious ego dissolution, visionary restructuralization; 15 item clusters) and Adjective Mood Rating Scale (AM; 14 scales), both completed 120 minutes after MDMA or placebo; duration of the subjective effect (method not described); side effects assessed during the session and 1 and 3 days later (reported separately).
outcomes.validity_norms: Established German-language scales (Dittrich 1985 and 1998; Janke and Debus 1978).
outcomes.operationalization: MANOVA for MDMA against placebo on the three ASC scales; two-way repeated-measures ANOVA with pretreatment (placebo or citalopram) and treatment (placebo or MDMA) as within-person factors, the interaction showing that citalopram changed the MDMA effect; Tukey post hoc tests for subscores; Wilcoxon matched-pairs tests for the AM scales; significance at P<0.05.
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: None across the 3 ASC scales, 15 ASC clusters and 14 AM scales (32 outcomes by the editors' count), each with several contrasts; Tukey tests only within ANOVAs.
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Described as double-blind; whether the blind held is not assessed; nausea in 6 of 16 after citalopram infusion (and fatigue, headache) could reveal the infusion.

analysis.effect_sizes: ASC item clusters, percent of maximum, mean for MDMA alone against citalopram then MDMA (n=16; Table 1): positive basic mood 40.1 against 16.4; derealization 32.7 against 12.6; depersonalization 24.5 against 10.5; alterations of the sense of time 30.9 against 13.1; mania-like experience 26.6 against 6.7; thought disorder 24.8 against 8.6; loss of thought control 14.1 against 2.8; loss of body control 11.9 against 5.3; changed meaning of percepts 37.3 against 14.1; facilitated imagination 27.2 against 6.6 (all marked significant); not significantly lowered: frightening derealization 8.5 against 2.1 (P<0.06), synesthesia 12.8 against 8.0, facilitated recollection 18.4 against 7.6; delusion and hallucinations were not significantly above placebo. Editors' percentage falls for the significant clusters: 55% to 80%. Pretreatment-by-treatment interactions: oceanic boundlessness F(1,15)=22.47, P<.0003; anxious ego dissolution F(1,15)=23.04, P<.0002; visionary restructuralization F(1,15)=12.80, P<.027 as printed (about 0.003 by the editors' calculation). Citalopram alone changed scores little (e.g., positive basic mood 2.3% against 0.6% on placebo). AM scales: MDMA raised heightened mood (P<.03), self-confidence (P<.02), extroversion (P<.01), introversion (P<.05), emotional excitability (P<.01), sensitivity (P<.03) and thoughtfulness (P<.002); citalopram lowered the MDMA-induced increases in self-confidence (P<.04) and extroversion (P<.01) to the level of citalopram alone and efficiency-activation (P<.03); the fall in heightened mood did not reach significance (P=.06); emotional excitability and sensitivity were not lowered at all. Time course: MDMA's subjective effect began 20 to 120 minutes after intake (mean 45), peaked 15 to 30 minutes later and lasted a mean of 3 hours; after citalopram the effect was 'markedly reduced but interestingly prolonged' to a mean of 5 hours (no test or spread given). The authors summarize the lowering as about 60% and note no correlation between citalopram dose per kg and the size of the lowering, and that in a pilot of two people 60 mg and 80 mg of citalopram blocked MDMA's effects to a degree comparable to 40 mg.
analysis.preregistration_detail: A 1999 study; no registry entry is mentioned.
analysis.selective_reporting: Cardiovascular, temperature, side-effect and startle results from the same sessions are reported in other papers (cited as submitted); no data are given for the duration finding or the pilot with 60 and 80 mg of citalopram.

interpretation_gap.results_show: In 16 healthy volunteers, mostly with no MDMA experience, 40 mg of citalopram by infusion before 1.5 mg/kg of MDMA lowered ratings of most altered-state clusters by roughly 55 to 80% (the authors say about 60%) 2 hours after MDMA, and lowered self-confidence, extroversion and efficiency-activation, but not emotional excitability or sensitivity; the effect lasted longer by the authors' account (5 hours against 3), without data. Nothing about blood levels was measured.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The authors conclude that citalopram attenuated MDMA's acute psychological effects by about 60% and that this suggests the psychoactive properties are largely dependent on action at the serotonin uptake site, with other mechanisms (dopamine, norepinephrine, receptors) accounting for the rest. They suggest the longer duration may be a metabolic interaction (citalopram inhibits CYP2D6) or competition at the uptake site; neither is tested here, and the study measured no blood levels.

timeline.event: Case series of four people who had taken fluoxetine before ecstasy (McCann and Ricaurte; cited here): one felt less effect and three no change; the authors of this study attribute the difference to the lower, oral fluoxetine dose

Independent group: paroxetine 20 mg a day for 3 days before MDMA lowered blood pressure, heart rate, pupil, temperature and subjective responses in 12 men while raising MDMA's peak by 16% and exposure by 22%

Systematic review: lowered effects were also reported for fluoxetine, duloxetine and reboxetine, with bupropion the exception for subjective ratings (as summarized by the review; the duloxetine and reboxetine trials are from this study's laboratory, the fluoxetine trial from another)

replication.where_it_stands: Blunting of MDMA's effects by serotonin reuptake inhibitors was seen again with paroxetine by an independent group (Barcelona) and, as cited in that paper and summarized by the 2022 review, with fluoxetine by another group; duloxetine and reboxetine trials summarized by the review come from this study's own laboratory. The duration finding (3 to 5 hours) was not examined with statistics here and is not reported as such in the paroxetine trial.

funding.funder: Heffter Research Institute, Santa Fe, New Mexico (Acknowledgments); citalopram ampoules 'kindly provided' by Lundbeck, Switzerland, the maker of citalopram (Substances and Dosing); MDMA from the Swiss Federal Health Office.
funding.declared_conflicts: None stated: the article carries no conflict-of-interest statement; the maker of citalopram supplied the drug.
funding.affiliations_note: Psychiatric University Hospital Zurich, research department. Liechti is also the last author of several of the later trials of medicines before MDMA that the 2022 review summarizes (reboxetine, duloxetine, methylphenidate, clonidine and others), so those trials and this one are one laboratory's work, not independent confirmations of each other.

what_would_settle_it: A randomized, double-blind crossover in people who take an SSRI for illness at steady state and in matched healthy volunteers, with MDMA concentrations and a measured time course of effects (so that duration can be tested and a pharmacokinetic cause separated from a pharmacodynamic one), more than one MDMA dose, women in numbers, a check that the blind held, and a second MDMA dose or a dose-choice task to find out what people do after feeling little and what their levels are then.

domains.note: Counterbalanced order of four conditions; the method is not described.
At least 14 days between sessions (citalopram half-life about 1.5 days).

Double-blind with saline infusion and placebo capsules, but nausea in 6 of 16 (and fatigue, headache) after citalopram could reveal the condition, MDMA's effects are obvious, and the blind was not tested.
All 16 volunteers are analysed on every outcome.
Self-rated scales at one time point (120 minutes) that could be influenced by partial unblinding; the duration of effect has no stated measurement method.
No registration; 32 scales and clusters tested without correction; cardiovascular and other results from the same sessions are reported elsewhere; no data for the duration finding.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: A counterbalanced, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover with a large and consistent effect across many scales, but 16 volunteers who were mostly drug-naive, subjective self-ratings with a blind that may have leaked, uncorrected multiple tests and no blood levels. The source can be cited for a roughly 60% lower rating of most psychological effects of 1.5 mg/kg MDMA 2 hours after an infusion of citalopram 40 mg, in 16 healthy volunteers; it cannot be cited for the longer duration, for people on long-term treatment, for blood levels, or for any effect on the amount taken or on harm.

key_findings.finding: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, within-person design with four counterbalanced conditions (placebo-placebo, citalopram-placebo, placebo-MDMA, citalopram-MDMA), sessions at least 14 days apart; citalopram 40 mg in saline over 90 minutes by infusion, then MDMA 1.5 mg/kg (mean 100 mg, SD 10) by mouth; psychometric ratings 120 minutes after MDMA.
key_findings.locator: Materials and Method > Substances and Dosing, 1st paragraph (p. 514); Study Design, 1st and 2nd paragraphs (pp. 514 to 515)

key_findings.finding: Sixteen volunteers, 12 men and 4 women, aged 21 to 39 (mean 27.4), high-school educated and nearly all university students or physicians; six had previous recreational drug experience, of whom three had tried ecstasy.

MDMA's subjective effect began 20 to 120 minutes after intake (mean 45), peaked 15 to 30 minutes later and lasted a mean of 3 hours; after citalopram the effect was markedly reduced but 'prolonged to a mean duration of 5 hours', with no measurement method, spread or test given; the Discussion says citalopram prolonged the effects 'by up to two hours' and offers a metabolic interaction (citalopram inhibits CYP2D6) or competition at the uptake site as possible reasons.
key_findings.locator: Results, 1st paragraph (p. 515); Discussion, paragraph beginning 'Another interesting finding' (p. 519)

key_findings.finding: ASC: MDMA raised all three scales against placebo (Rao R(3,12)=7.25, P<.005) and citalopram pretreatment lowered them (pretreatment by treatment: oceanic boundlessness F(1,15)=22.47, anxious ego dissolution F(1,15)=23.04, visionary restructuralization F(1,15)=12.80); positive basic mood 40.1% of maximum with MDMA against 16.4% after citalopram, derealization 32.7 against 12.6, thought disorder 24.8 against 8.6, changed meaning of percepts 37.3 against 14.1 (P<.05 for each cluster marked in Table 1).

AM: citalopram lowered the MDMA-induced rises in self-confidence (P<.04) and extroversion (P<.01) to the level of citalopram alone and lowered efficiency-activation (P<.03); the fall in heightened mood did not reach significance (P=.06); the rises in emotional excitability and sensitivity were not lowered at all.
key_findings.locator: Results, last paragraph (p. 516); Figure 2 (p. 518); Discussion, 2nd paragraph (p. 517)

key_findings.finding: Citalopram alone lowered some scale scores against placebo, which the authors attribute mostly to its side effects (fatigue, headache, nausea; nausea in 6 of 16); they argue this cannot explain the lowering seen in all subjects, and that in the same subjects citalopram also reduced MDMA's cardiovascular effects (reported elsewhere).
key_findings.locator: Discussion, 2nd paragraph (p. 517); paragraph beginning 'Non-specific untoward effects' (pp. 518 to 519)

key_findings.finding: The authors say citalopram attenuated MDMA's effects by about 60% only, which they do not attribute to too little citalopram: all received 40 mg whatever their weight, with no correlation between dose per kg and the size of the lowering, and in a pilot two people given 60 or 80 mg had MDMA's effects blocked to a degree comparable to 40 mg.

Conclusion: citalopram attenuated the acute psychological effects of MDMA in healthy humans by about 60%, suggesting the psychoactive properties of MDMA are largely dependent on action at the serotonin uptake site; other actions (dopamine, norepinephrine, receptors) are left open. A four-person case series of fluoxetine and ecstasy (one felt less effect, three no change) is discussed as differing in dose and route.
key_findings.locator: Abstract (p. 513); Introduction, last paragraph (pp. 513 to 514); Discussion, 1st to 3rd paragraphs (pp. 517 to 518) and concluding paragraph (pp. 519 to 520)

reporting_issues.issue: The duration finding (effect lasting 3 hours with MDMA alone and 5 hours after citalopram; 'up to two hours' longer) has no stated measurement method, no spread and no test, though it appears in the Results and is discussed as a finding.
reporting_issues.consequence: Treat it as an observation reported by the authors, not a tested result; with no blood levels, whether MDMA stayed longer in the blood (a CYP2D6 effect of citalopram) or its effect was delayed cannot be told.

reporting_issues.issue: The pretreatment-by-treatment result for visionary restructuralization is printed as F(1,15)=12.80, P<.027; that F value corresponds to about P=0.003, and F(1,15)=23.04 is printed with P<.0002 though it corresponds to about 0.00023 (the editors' calculation).
reporting_issues.consequence: Probably a dropped zero; the interaction is stronger than printed.

reporting_issues.issue: The authors' lowering of about 60 percent is given without saying how it was calculated; from the printed cluster means the significant falls are 55% to 80% (the editors' calculation), and some clusters were not significantly lowered.
reporting_issues.consequence: Use about 60 percent as the authors' summary, not as a measured average.

reporting_issues.issue: The argument that citalopram's own side effects (nausea in 6 of 16, fatigue, headache) are unlikely to explain the lowering rests on side-effect data that are 'to be reported separately'; the blind was not tested.
reporting_issues.consequence: Partial unblinding of the infusion could have influenced the ratings; the size of any such effect is unknown.

reporting_issues.issue: Cardiovascular, startle and side-effect results from the same sessions, and a pilot with 60 and 80 mg of citalopram in two people, are mentioned but not shown.
reporting_issues.consequence: The paper alone cannot be used for the cardiovascular effects or for the pilot's numbers.
